cond_0001.intro: The Credit Risk Data Scientist or Quantitative Analyst is responsible for developing consistent and coherent sets of models and analytical tools for credit risk measurement, management and reporting across [Company name masked]. Activities range from model design, development, implementation, and control designs used for understanding credit risk, such as portfolio stress testing and the Current Expected Credit Losses (CECL) accounting used for the Allowance for Credit Loss, and concentration correlation analyses. Partner with the Lines of Business, Accounting and Enterprise Risk functions to ensure that models and analytics address both internal and regulatory requirements.
cond_0001.responsibilities:
Responsible for developing, executing and preparing of supporting documentation for the quarterly Current Expected Credit Losses (CECL) calculation delivered to management.
Perform attribution analyses for model executions, and test for model assumptions and limitations, and assist in the ongoing monitoring of integrated model results.
Maintaining the CECL Documentation Library and Catalog to ensure that such documentation is available upon request by management, regulators, and internal and external auditors.
Monitoring the CECL calculation and execution workplan and schedule.
Assist in preparing quarterly CECL presentations to the Board of Directors.
Develop quantitative modeling other than CECL, such as loss forecasting, predictive risk rating models, stress testing, and profitability analysis.
Take the lead in developing and implementing predictive models, ad hoc analyses, visual/interactive reporting, segmentation analysis, and process automation. Identify the problem, provide potential solutions, and design the model construct.
Provide attention to detail and ensure data accuracy, reconciling and loading data.
Present findings and follow-up with business partners and executive management to ensure results understood and actionable.
Provide insightful analytical support for bank acquisitions and loan pool purchases.
Support external and internal audit and model risk management inquiries and supporting documentation.
Provide analytical insights to executive management and the board of directors on credit trends, including root cause analysis and potential solutions.
Proactively identify and evaluate emerging analytics software, technologies, and tools.
Self-motivated to proactively learn and solve complex business problems.
Strong ability to explain complex subject matter to a non-technical audience.
Strong attention to detail.
Excellent communication, interpersonal, organization, and time-management skills.
Ability to work in a fast-paced environment, manage competing priorities and to collaborate across the organization is essential.
cond_0001.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
7+ Years of relevant experience in developing, documenting, implementing, or validating quantitative models with concentration in financial domain.
Knowledge of multivariate statistics, machine learning, and predictive modelling.
Strong SAS programming skills, including SAS macro-language and SAS Visual Analytics.
Strong SQL programming skills.
Strong English communication skills, both written and verbal.
Preferred Requirements
MA/MS in Statistics or Quantitative field.
Knowledge of [Product name masked].
Prior Banking or Financial Services Experience.

cond_0010.intro: The Credit Risk Data Scientist or Quantitative Analyst is responsible for developing consistent and coherent sets of models and analytical tools for credit risk measurement, management and reporting across [Company name masked]. Activities range from model design, development, implementation, and control designs used for understanding credit risk, such as portfolio stress testing and the Current Expected Credit Losses (CECL) accounting used for the Allowance for Credit Loss, and concentration correlation analyses. Partner with the Lines of Business, Accounting and Enterprise Risk functions to ensure that models and analytics address both internal and regulatory requirements.
cond_0010.responsibilities:
Responsible for developing, executing and preparing of supporting documentation for the quarterly Current Expected Credit Losses (CECL) calculation delivered to management.
Perform attribution analyses for model executions, and test for model assumptions and limitations, and assist in the ongoing monitoring of integrated model results.
Maintaining the CECL Documentation Library and Catalog to ensure that such documentation is available upon request by management, regulators, and internal and external auditors.
Monitoring the CECL calculation and execution workplan and schedule.
Assist in preparing quarterly CECL presentations to the Board of Directors.
Develop quantitative modeling other than CECL, such as loss forecasting, predictive risk rating models, stress testing, and profitability analysis.
Take the lead in developing and implementing predictive models, ad hoc analyses, visual/interactive reporting, segmentation analysis, and process automation. Identify the problem, provide potential solutions, and design the model construct.
Provide attention to detail and ensure data accuracy, reconciling and loading data.
Present findings and follow-up with business partners and executive management to ensure results understood and actionable.
Provide insightful analytical support for bank acquisitions and loan pool purchases.
Support external and internal audit and model risk management inquiries and supporting documentation.
Provide analytical insights to executive management and the board of directors on credit trends, including root cause analysis and potential solutions.
Proactively identify and evaluate emerging analytics software, technologies, and tools.
Self-motivated to proactively learn and solve complex business problems.
Strong ability to explain complex subject matter to a non-technical audience.
Strong attention to detail.
Excellent communication, interpersonal, organization, and time-management skills.
Ability to work in a fast-paced environment, manage competing priorities and to collaborate across the organization is essential.
cond_0010.requirements:
7+ Years of relevant experience in developing, documenting, implementing, or validating quantitative models with concentration in financial domain.
MA/MS in Statistics or Quantitative field strongly preferred.
Knowledge of multivariate statistics, machine learning, and predictive modelling.
Strong SAS programming skills, including SAS macro-language and SAS Visual Analytics.
Strong SQL programming skills.
Knowledge of [Product name masked] beneficial.
Strong English communication skills, both written and verbal.
Prior Banking or Financial Services Experience Preferred.

cond_0019.intro: The Credit Risk Data Scientist or Quantitative Analyst is responsible for developing consistent and coherent sets of models and analytical tools for credit risk measurement, management and reporting across [Company name masked]. Activities range from model design, development, implementation, and control designs used for understanding credit risk, such as portfolio stress testing and the Current Expected Credit Losses (CECL) accounting used for the Allowance for Credit Loss, and concentration correlation analyses. Partner with the Lines of Business, Accounting and Enterprise Risk functions to ensure that models and analytics address both internal and regulatory requirements.
cond_0019.responsibilities:
Responsible for developing, executing and preparing of supporting documentation for the quarterly Current Expected Credit Losses (CECL) calculation delivered to management.
Perform attribution analyses for model executions, and test for model assumptions and limitations, and assist in the ongoing monitoring of integrated model results.
Maintaining the CECL Documentation Library and Catalog to ensure that such documentation is available upon request by management, regulators, and internal and external auditors.
Monitoring the CECL calculation and execution workplan and schedule.
Assist in preparing quarterly CECL presentations to the Board of Directors.
Develop quantitative modeling other than CECL, such as loss forecasting, predictive risk rating models, stress testing, and profitability analysis.
Take the lead in developing and implementing predictive models, ad hoc analyses, visual/interactive reporting, segmentation analysis, and process automation. Identify the problem, provide potential solutions, and design the model construct.
Provide attention to detail and ensure data accuracy, reconciling and loading data.
Present findings and follow-up with business partners and executive management to ensure results understood and actionable.
Provide insightful analytical support for bank acquisitions and loan pool purchases.
Support external and internal audit and model risk management inquiries and supporting documentation.
Provide analytical insights to executive management and the board of directors on credit trends, including root cause analysis and potential solutions.
Proactively identify and evaluate emerging analytics software, technologies, and tools.
Self-motivated to proactively learn and solve complex business problems.
Strong ability to explain complex subject matter to a non-technical audience.
Strong attention to detail.
Excellent communication, interpersonal, organization, and time-management skills.
Ability to work in a fast-paced environment, manage competing priorities and to collaborate across the organization is essential.
cond_0019.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
7+ Years of relevant experience in developing, documenting, implementing, or validating quantitative models with concentration in financial domain.
Knowledge of multivariate statistics, machine learning, and predictive modelling.
Strong SAS programming skills, including SAS macro-language and SAS Visual Analytics.
Strong SQL programming skills.
Strong English communication skills, both written and verbal.
Preferred Requirements
MA/MS in Statistics or Quantitative field.
Knowledge of [Product name masked].
Prior Banking or Financial Services Experience.

cond_0144.intro: We are looking for a Credit Risk Quantitative Analyst to join our team. This role involves working with colleagues across Lines of Business, Accounting, and Enterprise Risk to develop consistent and coherent sets of models and analytical tools for credit risk measurement, management, and reporting. Work spans model design, development, implementation, and control designs for understanding credit risk, including portfolio stress testing, Current Expected Credit Losses (CECL) accounting for the Allowance for Credit Loss, and concentration correlation analyses. You will coordinate with these functions to help ensure that models and analytics address both internal and regulatory requirements.
cond_0144.responsibilities:
Coordinate with stakeholders to develop, execute, and prepare supporting documentation for the quarterly Current Expected Credit Losses (CECL) calculation delivered to management.
Conduct attribution analyses for model executions, test for model assumptions and limitations, and support the ongoing monitoring of integrated model results.
Maintain the CECL Documentation Library and Catalog to ensure documentation is available upon request by management, regulators, and internal and external auditors.
Help monitor the CECL calculation and execution workplan and schedule.
Assist in preparing quarterly CECL presentations to the Board of Directors.
Work with the team to develop quantitative modeling beyond CECL, such as loss forecasting, predictive risk rating models, stress testing, and profitability analysis.
Coordinate with business partners to develop and implement predictive models, ad hoc analyses, visual/interactive reporting, segmentation analysis, and process automation. Help identify problems, contribute potential solutions, and support the design of model constructs.
Ensure data accuracy, reconciling and loading data with attention to detail.
Share findings and follow up with business partners and executive management to ensure results are understood and actionable.
Provide analytical support for bank acquisitions and loan pool purchases in coordination with relevant teams.
Support external and internal audit and model risk management inquiries and related documentation.
Share analytical insights with executive management and the board of directors on credit trends, including root cause analysis and potential solutions.
Work with the team to identify and evaluate emerging analytics software, technologies, and tools.
Contribute to solving complex business problems and support knowledge-sharing across the group.
Communicate complex subject matter clearly to non-technical audiences.
Maintain strong attention to detail and effective communication, interpersonal, organization, and time-management practices.
Collaborate across the organization while managing competing priorities.
cond_0144.requirements:
7+ Years of relevant experience in developing, documenting, implementing, or validating quantitative models with concentration in financial domain.
MA/MS in Statistics or Quantitative field strongly preferred.
Knowledge of multivariate statistics, machine learning, and predictive modelling.
Strong SAS programming skills, including SAS macro-language and SAS Visual Analytics.
Strong SQL programming skills.
Knowledge of [Product name masked] beneficial.
Strong English communication skills, both written and verbal.
Prior Banking or Financial Services Experience Preferred.

Activities range from model design, development, implementation, and control designs used for understanding credit risk, such as portfolio stress testing and the Current Expected Credit Losses (CECL) accounting used for the Allowance for Credit Loss, and concentration correlation analyses. Coordinate with Lines of Business, Accounting, and Enterprise Risk functions to ensure that models and analytics address both internal and regulatory requirements.
cond_0205.responsibilities:
Develop, execute, and prepare supporting documentation for the quarterly Current Expected Credit Losses (CECL) calculation delivered to management.
Perform attribution analyses for model executions, test for model assumptions and limitations, and assist in the ongoing monitoring of integrated model results.
Maintain the CECL Documentation Library and Catalog to ensure that documentation is available upon request by management, regulators, and internal and external auditors.
Monitor the CECL calculation and execution workplan and schedule.
Assist in preparing quarterly CECL materials for the Board of Directors.
Develop quantitative modeling other than CECL, such as loss forecasting, predictive risk rating models, stress testing, and profitability analysis.
Lead the development and implementation of predictive models, ad hoc analyses, visual/interactive reporting, segmentation analysis, and process automation. Identify the problem, provide potential solutions, and design the model construct.
Ensure data accuracy, reconciling and loading data.
Document findings and share results with business partners and executive management to ensure results are understood and actionable.
Provide analytical support for bank acquisitions and loan pool purchases.
Support external and internal audit and model risk management inquiries with relevant documentation.
Provide analytical insights to executive management and the board of directors on credit trends, including root cause analysis and potential solutions.
Identify and evaluate emerging analytics software, technologies, and tools.
Solve complex business problems independently.
Explain complex subject matter clearly to non-technical audiences.
Maintain strong attention to detail.
Manage competing priorities and coordinate across the organization as required.

Activities range from model design, development, implementation, and control designs used for understanding credit risk, such as portfolio stress testing and the Current Expected Credit Losses (CECL) accounting used for the Allowance for Credit Loss, and concentration correlation analyses. Partner with the Lines of Business, Accounting and Enterprise Risk functions to ensure that models and analytics address both internal and regulatory requirements.
cond_0262.responsibilities:
Responsible for developing, executing and preparing of supporting documentation for the quarterly Current Expected Credit Losses (CECL) calculation delivered to management.
Perform attribution analyses for model executions, and test for model assumptions and limitations, and assist in the ongoing monitoring of integrated model results.
Maintaining the CECL Documentation Library and Catalog to ensure that such documentation is available upon request by management, regulators, and internal and external auditors.
Monitoring the CECL calculation and execution workplan and schedule.
Assist in preparing quarterly CECL presentations to the Board of Directors.
Develop quantitative modeling other than CECL, such as loss forecasting, predictive risk rating models, stress testing, and profitability analysis.
Take the lead in developing and implementing predictive models, ad hoc analyses, visual/interactive reporting, segmentation analysis, and process automation. Identify the problem, provide potential solutions, and design the model construct.
Provide attention to detail and ensure data accuracy, reconciling and loading data.
Present findings and follow-up with business partners and executive management to ensure results understood and actionable.
Provide insightful analytical support for bank acquisitions and loan pool purchases.
Support external and internal audit and model risk management inquiries and supporting documentation.
Provide analytical insights to executive management and the board of directors on credit trends, including root cause analysis and potential solutions.
Proactively identify and evaluate emerging analytics software, technologies, and tools.
Self-motivated to proactively learn and solve complex business problems.
Strong ability to explain complex subject matter to a non-technical audience.
Strong attention to detail.
Excellent communication, interpersonal, organization, and time-management skills.
Ability to work in a fast-paced environment, manage competing priorities and to collaborate across the organization is essential.
cond_0262.requirements:
7+ Years of relevant experience in developing, documenting, implementing, or validating quantitative models with concentration in financial domain.
MA/MS in Statistics or Quantitative field strongly preferred.
Knowledge of multivariate statistics, machine learning, and predictive modelling.
Strong SAS programming skills, including SAS macro-language and SAS Visual Analytics.
Strong SQL programming skills.
Knowledge of [Product name masked] beneficial.
Strong English communication skills, both written and verbal.

cond_0290.intro: The Credit Risk Data Scientist or Quantitative Analyst is responsible for developing consistent and coherent sets of models and analytical tools for credit risk measurement, management and reporting across [Company name masked]. Activities range from model design, development, implementation, and control designs used for understanding credit risk, such as portfolio stress testing and the Current Expected Credit Losses (CECL) accounting used for the Allowance for Credit Loss, and concentration correlation analyses. Partner with the Lines of Business, Accounting and Enterprise Risk functions to ensure that models and analytics address both internal and regulatory requirements.
cond_0290.responsibilities:
Responsible for developing, executing and preparing of supporting documentation for the quarterly Current Expected Credit Losses (CECL) calculation delivered to management.
Perform attribution analyses for model executions, and test for model assumptions and limitations, and assist in the ongoing monitoring of integrated model results.
Maintaining the CECL Documentation Library and Catalog to ensure that such documentation is available upon request by management, regulators, and internal and external auditors.
Monitoring the CECL calculation and execution workplan and schedule.
Assist in preparing quarterly CECL presentations to the Board of Directors.
Develop quantitative modeling other than CECL, such as loss forecasting, predictive risk rating models, stress testing, and profitability analysis.
Take the lead in developing and implementing predictive models, ad hoc analyses, visual/interactive reporting, segmentation analysis, and process automation. Identify the problem, provide potential solutions, and design the model construct.
Provide attention to detail and ensure data accuracy, reconciling and loading data.
Present findings and follow-up with business partners and executive management to ensure results understood and actionable.
Provide insightful analytical support for bank acquisitions and loan pool purchases.
Support external and internal audit and model risk management inquiries and supporting documentation.
Provide analytical insights to executive management and the board of directors on credit trends, including root cause analysis and potential solutions.
Proactively identify and evaluate emerging analytics software, technologies, and tools.
Self-motivated to proactively learn and solve complex business problems.
Strong ability to explain complex subject matter to a non-technical audience.
Strong attention to detail.
Excellent communication, interpersonal, organization, and time-management skills.
Ability to work in a fast-paced environment, manage competing priorities and to collaborate across the organization is essential.

Lead preparation of quarterly CECL presentations to the Board of Directors.

Ensure data accuracy, reconciling and loading data with strong attention to detail.
Present findings and follow up with business partners and executive management to ensure results are understood and actionable.
Deliver analytical insights for bank acquisitions and loan pool purchases.
Manage responses to external and internal audit and model risk management inquiries, including supporting documentation.
Provide analytical insights to executive management and the board of directors on credit trends, including root cause analysis and potential solutions.
Proactively identify and evaluate emerging analytics software, technologies, and tools.
Solve complex business problems independently and take initiative in learning new methods.
Communicate complex subject matter clearly to non-technical audiences.
Manage competing priorities and collaborate across the organization.

You will direct work across model design, development, implementation, and control designs for understanding credit risk — including portfolio stress testing, Current Expected Credit Losses (CECL) accounting for the Allowance for Credit Loss, and concentration correlation analyses. You will lead engagement with Lines of Business, Accounting, and Enterprise Risk functions to ensure models and analytics meet both internal and regulatory requirements.
cond_0422.responsibilities:
Develop, execute, and take ownership of supporting documentation for the quarterly Current Expected Credit Losses (CECL) calculation delivered to management.
Lead attribution analyses for model executions, test for model assumptions and limitations, and drive ongoing monitoring of integrated model results.
Maintain the CECL Documentation Library and Catalog to ensure documentation is available upon request by management, regulators, and internal and external auditors.
Manage the CECL calculation and execution workplan and schedule.
Direct preparation of quarterly CECL presentations to the Board of Directors.
Develop quantitative modeling beyond CECL, including loss forecasting, predictive risk rating models, stress testing, and profitability analysis.
Lead the development and implementation of predictive models, ad hoc analyses, visual/interactive reporting, segmentation analysis, and process automation. Define the problem, determine potential solutions, and set the model construct.
Ensure data accuracy, reconciling and loading data with strong attention to detail.
Present findings and follow up with business partners and executive management to ensure results are understood and actionable.
Deliver analytical insights for bank acquisitions and loan pool purchases.
Manage external and internal audit and model risk management inquiries and supporting documentation.
Provide analytical insights to executive management and the board of directors on credit trends, including root cause analysis and potential solutions.
Proactively identify and evaluate emerging analytics software, technologies, and tools.
Self-motivated to proactively learn and solve complex business problems.
Strong ability to explain complex subject matter to a non-technical audience.
Strong attention to detail.
Excellent communication, interpersonal, organization, and time-management skills.
Ability to manage competing priorities and collaborate across the organization.
cond_0422.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
7+ Years of relevant experience developing, documenting, implementing, or validating quantitative models in a financial domain.
Strong SAS programming skills, including SAS macro-language and SAS Visual Analytics.
Strong SQL programming skills.
Knowledge of multivariate statistics, machine learning, and predictive modelling.
Strong English communication skills, both written and verbal.
Preferred Requirements
MA/MS in Statistics or a quantitative field.
Prior banking or financial services experience.
Knowledge of [Product name masked].
cond_0422.values: We value achievement, high standards, and work that is carried out with real discipline. We believe strong organizations are defined by the quality of what they deliver.

cond_0462.intro: We are looking for a Credit Risk Quantitative Analyst to join our team.
cond_0462.responsibilities:
Responsible for developing, executing and preparing of supporting documentation for the quarterly Current Expected Credit Losses (CECL) calculation delivered to management.
Perform attribution analyses for model executions, and test for model assumptions and limitations, and assist in the ongoing monitoring of integrated model results.
Maintaining the CECL Documentation Library and Catalog to ensure that such documentation is available upon request by management, regulators, and internal and external auditors.
Monitoring the CECL calculation and execution workplan and schedule.
Assist in preparing quarterly CECL presentations to the Board of Directors.
Develop quantitative modeling other than CECL, such as loss forecasting, predictive risk rating models, stress testing, and profitability analysis.
Take the lead in developing and implementing predictive models, ad hoc analyses, visual/interactive reporting, segmentation analysis, and process automation. Identify the problem, provide potential solutions, and design the model construct.
Provide attention to detail and ensure data accuracy, reconciling and loading data.
Present findings and follow-up with business partners and executive management to ensure results understood and actionable.
Provide insightful analytical support for bank acquisitions and loan pool purchases.
Support external and internal audit and model risk management inquiries and supporting documentation.
Provide analytical insights to executive management and the board of directors on credit trends, including root cause analysis and potential solutions.
Proactively identify and evaluate emerging analytics software, technologies, and tools.
Self-motivated to proactively learn and solve complex business problems.
Strong ability to explain complex subject matter to a non-technical audience.
Strong attention to detail.
Excellent communication, interpersonal, organization, and time-management skills.
Ability to work in a fast-paced environment, manage competing priorities and to collaborate across the organization is essential.
cond_0462.requirements:
Around 7 years of experience in developing, documenting, implementing, or validating quantitative models, ideally with a focus in the financial domain, or an equivalent combination of education and experience.

Provide insightful analytical support for bank acquisitions and loan pool purchases.
Support external and internal audit and model risk management inquiries and supporting documentation.
Provide analytical insights to executive management and the board of directors on credit trends, including root cause analysis and potential solutions.
Proactively identify and evaluate emerging analytics software, technologies, and tools.
Self-motivated to proactively learn and solve complex business problems.
Strong ability to explain complex subject matter to a non-technical audience.
Strong attention to detail.
Excellent communication, interpersonal, organization, and time-management skills.
Ability to work in a fast-paced environment, manage competing priorities and to collaborate across the organization is essential.
